principles.text: Sell before you build: do at least 50 discovery calls and look for people who will prepay before writing code.
Without word of mouth nothing you do will work; with it, ads, email and outbound all speed growth up.
People do business with people, not companies: build a founder brand and expect about a year to find your voice.
Connect with your ICP, let them see your content for 60 days, then ask for a meeting.
Don't hire anyone before $1M ARR; aim for $10M ARR with 10 or fewer employees and no VC money.

sampleQA.question: How should I validate a SaaS idea before building it?

answer.text: Commit to at least 50 discovery calls. The only goal is finding people who will pay for something you haven't built yet.
Ask how they handle the problem today and what their team complains about, not whether they like your idea.
Money is the honest signal. If people pay for a rough version that sucks, that's indicator one to pursue it.

sampleQA.question: How do I use LinkedIn to get customers as a founder?

answer.text: Post from your personal profile on 2-3 authentic, non-mainstream pillars tangential to the problem you solve.
Spend most effort on the hook: write as if no one knows you, build credibility fast, use numbers.
Run connect campaigns to your ICP, don't pitch, wait about 60 days, then reach out. He reports an 80% reply rate.
Expect it to take about a year before it clicks.

sampleQA.question: Should I raise VC for my SaaS?

answer.text: He talked to 50+ VC firms about his $25M ARR business and decided never to take VC, citing dividends and control.
A lean company at $10M ARR is the promised land: total optionality, and you can sell or keep it from strength.
Create product pull first; money raised too early gets spent on channels before there is pull.
When he tried to scale Retention.com like a VC-backed company, hiring 50 people in 60 days, it failed.
